biography: Casey Mears, a name synonymous with aggressive American racing, clawed his way from the dusty short tracks of Bakersfield to the hallowed grounds of international motorsport. Unlike many drivers born into racing dynasties, Casey's journey began with a beat-up go-kart scavenged from a junkyard. His relentless pursuit of speed saw him dominating local races, earning him the moniker 'The Bakersfield Bandit'. A defining moment came at the '98 Kern County Raceway, where, after starting last due to a blown engine in qualifying, Mears carved through the field, executing a daring last-lap pass for the win, a move that caught the eye of Reynard Racing. Now, at 31, Mears finds himself at the peak of his career, battling for championships and etching his name into racing lore, one aggressive maneuver at a time.
drivingStyle: Mears is known for his late-braking maneuvers and an uncanny ability to extract every last ounce of performance from his car. He's a master of the 'dive bomb,' often catching rivals off guard with his aggressive corner entry. While some criticize his style as reckless, Mears maintains that it's simply 'maximum efficiency.' He's a driver who thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest. Tire management is not his strong suit; he prefers to push hard early, often relying on his raw speed to compensate for late-race degradation.
